This page lets you rebuild the structure of `src/scgsim` from one place: which
stages exist, the order the work flows through them on the Palace route and on
the AEDT route, what crosses from one stage to the next, and which folder is
which stage. A *stage* is a folder that takes what an earlier stage produced
and produces what a later stage reads. The tables on this page are generated
from the folders' own docstrings, so they say what the code says.

## The two routes {#routes}

The two routes are those of the [backend support matrix](backend-support.qmd),
and both end at a result a person reads. The Palace route starts from a layout
and a stack. The AEDT route has two entries. Every AEDT calculation accepts an
AEDT request spec passed to `prepare_handoff`: the caller builds the spec
records of `aedt/specs`, and Q2D and source-free Q3D enter only this way.
Source-first HFSS Eigenmode and the Q3D C/G preparation can start from a
`GeometryPlan` instead; its snapshot passes through the shared geometry stages
and `geometry/planning` before `aedt/preparation`.
Every square box is a folder below `src/scgsim`, named as the folder is; a
rounded box is outside SCGSim. A solid arrow is an import: the stage at its
head imports the stage at its tail, or, where the arrow says *calls*, the stage
at its tail calls the one at its head. A dashed arrow is a file or a value
handed over, labelled with what it is and, where a contract module defines the
file, with that module. The inner Palace box holds what `palace/simulation`
runs when a notebook calls `mesh()`, `write_config()` and `prepare_handoff()`.

```{mermaid}
%%| column: screen-inset
flowchart TB
  layout(["layout and stack"]) -. "components or GDS, stack" .-> gsource
  subgraph shared["shared geometry"]
    gsource["geometry/source"] --> ginterp["geometry/interpretation"]
    ginterp -- "calls as its last step" --> gjunc["geometry/junctions"]
  end
  ginterp --> psource
  ginterp --> gplan
  subgraph palace_route["Palace route"]
    subgraph simulation["run by palace/simulation"]
      psource["palace/source"] --> pmesh["palace/mesh"]
      pmesh -- "calls" --> gsepr["geometry/surface_epr"]
      gsepr -- "calls" --> gsgb["geometry/sgb"]
      gsgb -. "XAO and sidecar<br/>contracts/sgb_sidecar" .-> meshing["meshing"]
      pmesh -- "calls" --> meshing
      pmesh --> pconfig["palace/config"]
      pconfig -. "config.json<br/>contracts/palace_run_folder" .-> prun["palace/run"]
    end
    prun -. "run folder" .-> palace_solver(["Palace"])
    palace_solver -. "returned run folder<br/>contracts/palace_run_folder" .-> presults["palace/results"]
    presults --> preports["palace/reports"]
  end
  subgraph aedt_route["AEDT route"]
    subgraph plan_backed["GeometryPlan entry"]
      gplan["geometry/planning"]
    end
    request(["request values"]) -. "AEDT request spec<br/>every family; the only entry for Q2D and source-free Q3D" .-> aspecs
    gplan --> aprep
    aspecs["aedt/specs"] --> aprep["aedt/preparation"]
    aprep -. "handoff folder" .-> aruntime["aedt/runtime"]
    aruntime -- "calls" --> aepr["aedt/epr"]
    gplan --> aepr
    aruntime -. "run folder and receipt" .-> aresults["aedt/results"]
    aepr --> aresults
    aresults -- "calls" --> apres["aedt/presentation"]
  end
```

The diagram leaves out the folders every stage of an area uses:
`geometry/models`, `geometry/exact` and `geometry/grid` in geometry, `geometry/sgb/records` in SGB,
and `semantics` and `presentation` across the package. AEDT's handoff and
receipt formats are defined in `aedt/specs` and `aedt/results`, not in
`contracts`. `visualization` reads a Palace run folder or an AEDT project to
draw a geometry preview; it is not a step of either route. The stage tables
below list every folder.

## How to read a folder {#read-a-folder}

Every package folder's `__init__.py` opens with one sentence that says what the
folder is. A stage folder adds three lines:

```text
<one sentence: what the folder is>

In: what the stage takes, and from which stage
Out: what the stage produces
Next: which stage reads that
```

Imports point against the flow: a later stage imports an earlier one, and an
earlier stage does not import a later one. The exception is a stage that
drives others: `palace/simulation` imports each Palace stage it runs,
`geometry/interpretation` calls `geometry/junctions` as its last step, and
`aedt/runtime` calls the in-AEDT part of `aedt/epr`. These imports also point
from an earlier stage to a later one:

| Importing folder | Imports | What it takes from there |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `aedt/specs` | `aedt/epr` | The grouping of surface integrals (`epr.selection`). |
| `aedt/preparation` | `aedt/results` | The receipt schema and the initial receipt (`results.provenance`). |
| `aedt/results` | `aedt/runtime`, `aedt/epr`, `aedt/presentation` | The batch collection context and benchmark path, the `EprResult` record, and the display a `ResolvedRun` calls. |

## The order CI checks {#checked-order}

A folder reads only the folders before it in its list. The quality gate checks
each list (`.importlinter`), and each list is complete: a new folder has to be
given its place in the order before CI passes.

| Where | The order, earliest first |
| --- | --- |
| The package | `contracts`, `refusal`, `documentation` → `preparation`, `diagnostics` → `semantics` → `presentation` → `geometry` → `meshing` → `palace` and `aedt` → `visualization` |
| `geometry` | `models` → `exact` → `grid` → `source` → `junctions` → `interpretation` → `planning` (AEDT only) |
| `geometry/sgb` | `errors`, `stopwatch` → `records` → `prisms` → `arrangement` → `bands` → `topology` → `checks` → `model` → `output` → `section` → `build` |
| `palace` | `source` → `mesh` → `config` → `run` → `results` → `reports`; the `simulation` classes are the entry |

Folders written with a comma or "and" in one step do not read each other.
Four statements are stricter than an order, and CI checks them too:

- SGB reads `geometry/models` and `geometry/exact` and no other geometry folder,
  and no folder before SGB reads it. The stages hand SGB data, not code;
  `geometry/surface_epr` and the Palace backend call it.
- `geometry/exact` reads `geometry/models` only, so exact arithmetic never rests
  on the float grid operations of `geometry/grid`.
- `meshing` reads the sidecar and the XAO through `contracts`, never SGB or a
  backend (one constant of `geometry/models/grid` is the stated exception);
  `visualization` reads a Palace run folder the same way.
- `contracts` imports nothing else from `scgsim` and no third-party package.

SGB's list is the order of dependency, not of time. In time the arrangement
runs twice: on the physical prisms alone, where `bands` finds its support
faces, then with the cut families `bands` produces. The step list of
`geometry/sgb/model.py` is the order in time.

AEDT's stage folders are not in a checked order; the table under
[How to read a folder](#read-a-folder) lists the imports that point against
the flow there.

## Stage tables {#stage-tables}

Each area has one table, its rows in the order the work flows through it. A
row's text is the folder's docstring: *What it is* is the first sentence, and
In, Out and Next are the three lines. A folder that is not a stage says in
its In cell what it is instead: an area's own folder, or a part of the stage
in the row it names.

To change a row, edit the folder's docstring, translate the changed text in
`scripts/code_map_zh_tw.toml`, and run `python scripts/generate_code_map.py`;
the order of the rows is stated once, in that script. Each entry of the
translation file records the English it translates. The script refuses a
package folder it does not list, a stage whose docstring lacks one of the three
lines, a folder without a translation entry, an entry for a folder that is gone,
and an entry whose recorded English is no longer the docstring's text; that
refusal prints the new English to record and translate.
`tests/test_code_map.py` fails while the tables differ from the docstrings and
their translations.

{{< include _code-map-stages.md >}}

## Top-level modules {#top-level-modules}

Four modules sit directly in `src/scgsim`, outside every area's folders. They
are not stages; a stage calls them.

| Module | What it is | Called by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `preparation.py` | The worker budget of geometry preparation: one thread pool shared by the preparation calls in a `preparation_resources` scope. | `geometry` and `palace/mesh` |
| `diagnostics.py` | Opt-in timing, progress, memory and profile records of a preparation, written beside the result. | `geometry` and `palace/mesh` |
| `documentation.py` | Links from a message to the published documentation of the version that raised it. | `geometry` |
| `refusal.py` | The wording of a refusal: the two sentence shapes, the declared object a refusal names, and the text of a value found. | every folder except `contracts` |

A refusal takes one of two shapes: "{object}: {problem}. Change it in
{where}." for input the caller can change, and "internal: {invariant}.
Nothing in the input is to blame: report it to SCGSim with the input that
produced it." for a broken promise of SCGSim's own. `refusal.py` words both,
and every folder builds its refusals with it; `contracts` imports nothing from
`scgsim` and keeps its own literals.

## Ambient state {#ambient-state}

Everything a result or a message depends on is an argument or a return value.
What is held in a context variable instead is listed here; none of it can
change a result.

| Where | What it holds | Why it may be ambient |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `preparation.py` `_state` | The worker budget and its thread pool. | Maps keep input order, so the budget changes only how many threads run them. |
| `preparation.py` `_worker_depth` | How deep a map runs inside a worker. | It only makes a nested map run serially. |
| `diagnostics.py` `_recorder` | The open diagnostic recorder. | It writes timing and memory files beside a result; nothing reads it back. |
| `diagnostics.py` `_span` | The open timing span. | It names the parent of the next timing record only. |
| `geometry/grid/grid_cache.py` `ACTIVE` | Pure subdivision work already done in this call. | A cache: a hit returns what the work would compute. |
| `geometry/source/occurrence.py` `_EXTRACTION_CACHE` | Polygons already extracted from one source library. | A cache: a hit returns what the extraction would compute. |

## Where to put new code {#new-code}

- A helper lives in the earliest stage that calls it, and later stages import
  it from there.
- What only AEDT's native construction calls lives in `geometry/planning`;
  nothing on the Palace route imports that folder.
- `geometry/models` imports no other geometry code, and `contracts` imports
  nothing else from `scgsim` and no third-party package, so every stage can
  import them. The import-linter contract `contracts-import-nothing-else`
  checks `contracts`.
- A new package folder goes into `AREAS` in `scripts/generate_code_map.py`
  where the work reaches it, with the sentence and, for a stage, the three
  lines in its `__init__.py`, and their translation in
  `scripts/code_map_zh_tw.toml`.
